verses.text: David counted the men who were with him and put commanders over groups of a thousand and groups of a hundred.

He sent the army out in three groups. Joab led one third, Joab's brother Abishai son of Zeruiah led another third, and Ittai the Gittite led the last third. The king told the soldiers, "I will certainly go out with you myself."

But the men said, "You must not go out. If we have to run away, they won't care about us. Even if half of us die, they won't care. But you are worth ten thousand of us. So it is better for you to stay in the city and be ready to send us help."
The king said to them, "I will do whatever you think is best." So the king stood beside the city gate while all the army marched out in groups of hundreds and thousands.
The king gave an order to Joab, Abishai, and Ittai: "For my sake, be gentle with the young man Absalom." All the soldiers heard the king give this order to the commanders about Absalom.
So David's army went out into the countryside to fight against Israel, and the battle took place in the forest of Ephraim.
There the army of Israel was defeated by David's men. A great many were killed that day, twenty thousand men.
The battle spread out over the whole countryside, and the forest killed more people that day than the sword did.

Then Absalom happened to meet some of David's men. Absalom was riding his mule, and the mule went under the thick branches of a large oak tree. Absalom's head got caught in the tree, and he was left hanging in mid-air while the mule kept going.
One of the men saw this and told Joab, "I just saw Absalom hanging in an oak tree."
Joab said to the man who told him, "You saw him? Then why didn't you strike him down to the ground right there? I would have given you ten pieces of silver and a soldier's belt."

But the man said to Joab, "Even if I were given a thousand pieces of silver, I would not lift my hand against the king's son. We all heard the king order you, Abishai, and Ittai, 'For my sake, make sure no one harms the young man Absalom.'
If I had betrayed the king and killed his son, the king would have found out, because nothing is hidden from the king. And you would not have stood up for me."
Joab said, "I'm not going to waste time with you." So he took three spears in his hand and plunged them into Absalom's heart while he was still alive, hanging in the oak tree.
Then ten young men who carried Joab's armour surrounded Absalom, struck him, and killed him.
Then Joab blew the trumpet, and his men stopped chasing Israel, because Joab held them back.
They took Absalom's body, threw it into a large pit in the forest, and piled a huge heap of stones over it. Meanwhile, all the Israelites ran away to their own homes.

While Absalom was still alive, he had set up a stone pillar for himself in the King's Valley. He said, "I have no son to keep my name alive." So he named the pillar after himself, and it is still called Absalom's Monument today.
Then Ahimaaz son of Zadok said, "Let me run and take the good news to the king that the LORD has rescued him from his enemies."
Joab told him, "You are not the one to take the news today. You can do it another day, but not today, because the king's son is dead."
Then Joab said to a man from Cush, "Go and tell the king what you have seen." The man from Cush bowed down to Joab and ran off.
But Ahimaaz son of Zadok said to Joab again, "No matter what happens, please let me run after the man from Cush." Joab said, "My son, why do you want to go? You will get no reward for this news."
He answered, "No matter what happens, I want to run." So Joab said, "Run!" Then Ahimaaz ran by the road through the plain and passed the man from Cush.
David was sitting between the inner and outer gates of the city. The watchman went up to the roof over the gate by the wall. As he looked out, he saw a man running alone.
The watchman called out and told the king. The king said, "If he is alone, he must be bringing news." The runner came closer and closer.
Then the watchman saw another man running. He called down to the gatekeeper, "Look, another man is running alone!" The king said, "He must be bringing news too."
The watchman said, "I think the first man runs like Ahimaaz son of Zadok." The king said, "He is a good man. He must be bringing good news."

Ahimaaz called out to the king, "All is well!" He bowed down before the king with his face to the ground and said, "Praise the LORD your God! He has handed over the men who rebelled against my lord the king."
The king asked, "Is the young man Absalom safe?" Ahimaaz answered, "When Joab sent me, your servant, I saw a great commotion, but I don't know what it was about."
The king said, "Step aside and stand here." So he stepped aside and stood there.
Then the man from Cush arrived and said, "Good news for my lord the king! Today the LORD has rescued you from all who rose up against you."
The king asked the man from Cush, "Is the young man Absalom safe?" The man from Cush answered, "May all the enemies of my lord the king, and all who rise up to harm you, end up like that young man!"
The king was deeply shaken. He went up to the room over the gate and cried. As he went, he said, "My son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! If only I had died instead of you! Absalom, my son, my son!"
